items.description: The Great Mosque of Samarra was once the largest mosque in the world, commissioned by the Abbasid caliph Al-Mutawakkil in the 9th century.
facts: Completed in 851 AD
Famous for its 52-meter Malwiya spiral minaret
Constructed entirely of baked brick
UNESCO World Heritage site since 2007

items.description: Cheekha Dar is the highest mountain peak in Iraq, situated in the Zagros mountain range on the border with Iran.
facts: Elevation of 3,611 meters
Name translates to Black Tent in Kurdish
Located in the Erbil Governorate
Permanently covered in snow during winter months

items.description: The Al-Jazira Plateau is an upland region in northwestern Iraq situated between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.
facts: Part of the larger Mesopotamian region
Characterized by rolling hills and dry plains
Elevations range from 200 to 450 meters
Contains the Tharthar and Habbaniya lakes

items.description: The Southern Desert of Iraq, known as Al-Badiyah Al-Janubiyah, is a vast limestone plateau extending to the borders of Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.
facts: Covers roughly 15 percent of Iraq's land area
Features numerous seasonal wadis and depressions
Composed primarily of flat rocky plains and sand dunes
Subject to extreme temperature fluctuations

items.description: The Bahr al-Najaf is a large depression and seasonal lake located west of the city of Najaf, forming a unique ecosystem in the desert.
facts: Covers an area of approximately 360 square kilometers
Fed by seasonal rains and groundwater
Historically part of a larger ancient sea
Important stop for migratory birds
